paragraphs.raw_text: VELORAX 20 MG FILM-COATED TABLETS - STABILITY STUDY REPORT SR-2027-014

This is a synthetic stability report and closed factual record for testing document extraction. All products, companies, people and results are fictional. Apply only the rules stated in this report; where the narrative of the report and its tables differ, the tables record the measured results.
Prepared by Halden Therapeutics AS, Quality Control Stability Unit, on 15 March 2027, and approved by Ingrid Moe, Head of Quality Control.

1.1 This report presents the results of the registration stability study of Velorax (ralmetanib) 20 mg film-coated tablets up to 12 months at the long-term condition, and proposes a shelf life and a storage statement for each container closure system.
1.2 Three batches were placed on stability, one in each container closure system intended for marketing.
| Batch | Scale | Container closure system | Manufactured | Placed on stability |
| V20-2601 | Pilot, 100 000 tablets | HDPE bottle with desiccant | 12 January 2026 | 26 January 2026 |
| V20-2604 | Production, 1 000 000 tablets | PVC/Alu blister | 2 February 2026 | 9 February 2026 |
| V20-2607 | Production, 1 000 000 tablets | Alu/Alu blister | 23 February 2026 | 2 March 2026 |

2.1 Each batch is tested at release against the release specification, and each stability sample against the shelf-life specification. The two specifications list the same tests; their acceptance criteria differ.
| Appearance | White, round, biconvex film-coated tablets |
| Assay | 95.0 to 105.0 % of the label claim |
| Dissolution | Not less than 80 % (mean of 6 units) in 30 minutes |
| Appearance | White, round, biconvex film-coated tablets |
| Assay | 92.0 to 105.0 % of the label claim |
| Dissolution | Not less than 75 % (mean of 6 units) in 30 minutes |

2.2 A result is outside the shelf-life specification if it does not meet the acceptance criterion of Table 3 for its test. Each result outside the shelf-life specification is investigated under procedure QC-SOP-112, and the investigation is reported in section 5.

3.1 Samples of each batch were placed at the three conditions on the day on which the batch was placed on stability (Table 1). Time 0 is that day; the initial results of a batch are those of its time 0, and apply to every condition.

3.2 The samples at the intermediate condition are tested only for a batch that shows a significant change at the accelerated condition, at each of their time points from the time point at which the significant change is found.

3.3 A significant change at the accelerated condition is any of: a change in assay of 5.0 % of the label claim or more from the initial value; a result for impurity D or for total impurities outside the shelf-life specification; a water content outside the shelf-life specification; a dissolution result outside the shelf-life specification.

3.4 Assay is reported in % of the label claim, impurity D, total impurities and water content in % (w/w), and dissolution as the mean of 6 units in % dissolved after 30 minutes. Appearance complied at every time point of every batch and condition, and is not tabulated.
| Test | Initial | 3 months | 6 months | 9 months | 12 months |
| Test | Initial | 1 month | 2 months | 3 months | 6 months |
4.1.1 V20-2601 meets the shelf-life specification at every time point, and shows no significant change at the accelerated condition.
| Test | Initial | 3 months | 6 months | 9 months | 12 months |
| Test | Initial | 1 month | 2 months | 3 months | 6 months |

4.2.1 V20-2604 showed a significant change at the accelerated condition at 6 months (section 5). Its samples at the intermediate condition were tested from 6 months, and meet the shelf-life specification up to 12 months.
| Test | Initial | 3 months | 6 months | 9 months | 12 months |
| Test | Initial | 1 month | 2 months | 3 months | 6 months |
4.3.1 V20-2607 meets the shelf-life specification at every time point, and shows no significant change at the accelerated condition.

5.1 Investigation INV-26-031 was opened on 18 August 2026 for the 6-month results of V20-2604 at the accelerated condition, the first results of the study outside the shelf-life specification: impurity D, total impurities and water content.
5.2 The results were confirmed by retesting retained samples. A laboratory error was excluded: the system suitability, the reference standards and the sample preparation met their requirements.

5.3 Root cause: moisture ingress through the PVC film of the blister at 75 % RH. The water content of the tablets rose with the time of storage, and impurity D, a hydrolysis product, rose with it. At its intended storage of 25 °C/60 % RH the same batch stays within the shelf-life specification.

5.4 Corrective action: the PVC/Alu blister is not to be stored above 25 °C, and its storage statement requires protection from moisture. No action is needed for the HDPE bottle with desiccant or for the Alu/Alu blister.
5.5 INV-26-031 was closed on 30 September 2026. No other result of the study was outside the shelf-life specification.
6.1 Where no significant change occurs at the accelerated condition, the shelf life may be extrapolated to twice the period covered by the long-term data, and not beyond 24 months.

6.2 Where a significant change occurs at the accelerated condition and no significant change occurs at the intermediate condition, the shelf life may be extrapolated to one and a half times the period covered by the long-term data, and not more than 6 months beyond it.

6.3 Where a significant change occurs at the intermediate condition, or where it occurs at the accelerated condition and the intermediate condition has not been tested, the shelf life is not extended beyond the period covered by the long-term data.
6.4 A significant change at the intermediate condition is defined as at the accelerated condition (3.3).

6.5 The long-term data cover 12 months for each batch. The assay of each batch at the long-term condition decreases by no more than 0.15 % of the label claim per month, so that the assay of no batch is expected to fall below the shelf-life specification within 24 months.
Table 12. Proposed shelf lives and storage statements
| Container closure system | Batch | Proposed shelf life | Storage statement |
| HDPE bottle with desiccant | V20-2601 | 24 months | Do not store above 30 °C. |
| PVC/Alu blister | V20-2604 | 18 months | Do not store above 25 °C. Store in the original package in order to protect from moisture. |
| Alu/Alu blister | V20-2607 | 24 months | Do not store above 30 °C. |
7.1 The long-term study of the three batches continues to 36 months, and the results at 18, 24 and 36 months will be reported in updates of this report.
7.2 The first three production batches of each container closure system will be placed on stability at the long-term and accelerated conditions after approval.

7.3 The shelf life of each container closure system will be confirmed against the long-term data as they become available, and a result outside the shelf-life specification will be reported to the competent authorities within 30 days.
| Assay | HPLC with UV detection, AM-201 | Not applicable |
| Impurity D | HPLC with UV detection, AM-202 | 0.02 % |
| Total impurities | HPLC with UV detection, AM-202 | 0.02 % |
| Dissolution | Paddle apparatus at 50 rpm, 900 ml of pH 6.8 buffer, AM-203 | Not applicable |
| Water content | Coulometric Karl Fischer titration, AM-204 | Not applicable |

custom_data.review_scope: All 18 concept targets and four aspect selections authored with the case; the results outside the shelf-life specification, the significant changes and the extrapolated shelf lives recomputed by script.
custom_data.evidence_policy: Select the specification rows, results, rules and statements needed by the target. Exclude headings, table captions and table column headers. Nested concept evidence lies within its aspect.

concepts.name: Batches on stability
concepts.description: One object per batch placed on stability: its batch number (e.g. V20-2601), its scale, and its container closure system

structure.container_closure_system: literal["HDPE bottle with desiccant", "PVC/Alu blister", "Alu/Alu blister"]

items.justification: Table 1 lists V20-2601 as a pilot batch of 100 000 tablets in the HDPE bottle with desiccant.
Table 1 lists V20-2604 as a production batch of 1 000 000 tablets in the PVC/Alu blister.
Table 1 lists V20-2607 as a production batch of 1 000 000 tablets in the Alu/Alu blister.

concepts.name: Batches with a significant change at the accelerated condition
concepts.description: Select every batch whose results at 40 °C/75 % RH show a significant change as section 3.3 defines it, from the results in the tables, whatever the narrative of the report says

items.justification: At 40 °C/75 % RH, V20-2604 has a water content of 4.4 % at 3 months, above the 4.0 % of the shelf-life specification, and later an assay 5.8 % below its initial value and impurity D, total impurities and water content outside the specification; V20-2607 has 0.31 % of impurity D at 6 months, above 0.30 %, although 4.3.1 says it shows no significant change. V20-2601 stays within.

concepts.name: Shelf life supported for the Alu/Alu blister by the rules of section 6 in months
concepts.description: The longest shelf life, in months, that the rules of section 6 allow for the Alu/Alu blister, applied to the results in the tables, whatever the report proposes

items.justification: The Alu/Alu blister is batch V20-2607, whose impurity D of 0.31 % at 6 months at 40 °C/75 % RH is above the 0.30 % limit: a significant change by 3.3. Its intermediate samples were not tested, so 6.3 limits the shelf life to the 12 months of long-term data, not the proposed 24 months.

concepts.name: The conclusion on V20-2607 at the accelerated condition agrees with its results
concepts.description: Whether what the report concludes about batch V20-2607 at 40 °C/75 % RH agrees with its results in the tables

items.justification: 4.3.1 says that V20-2607 meets the shelf-life specification and shows no significant change at the accelerated condition, but Table 11 gives 0.31 % of impurity D at 6 months, above the 0.30 % limit of Table 3.

concepts.name: Date on which V20-2604 was placed at the intermediate condition
concepts.description: The date on which the samples of batch V20-2604 were placed at 30 °C/65 % RH

items.justification: Samples of each batch were placed at the three conditions on the day the batch was placed on stability, which Table 1 gives as 9 February 2026 for V20-2604.

aspects.name: Shelf-life acceptance criteria
aspects.description: Identify the acceptance criteria that the stability samples are tested against, and the rule on results that do not meet them. Leave out the release specification.

concepts.name: Shelf-life limit of impurity D in %
concepts.description: The highest content of impurity D, in %, that the shelf-life specification accepts

items.justification: Table 3, the shelf-life specification, accepts not more than 0.30 % of impurity D; 0.20 % is the limit of the release specification.

concepts.name: Shelf-life limit of water content in %
concepts.description: The highest water content, in %, that the shelf-life specification accepts

items.justification: Table 3, the shelf-life specification, accepts a water content of not more than 4.0 %; 3.0 % is the limit of the release specification.

concepts.name: Lower shelf-life limit of assay in %
concepts.description: The lowest assay, in % of the label claim, that the shelf-life specification accepts

items.justification: Table 3, the shelf-life specification, accepts an assay of 92.0 to 105.0 % of the label claim; the release specification starts at 95.0 %.

aspects.name: Stability results of V20-2604
aspects.description: Identify the results of batch V20-2604, in the PVC/Alu blister, at each storage condition, and the conclusions that the report draws from them in sections 4 and 5.

concepts.name: Total impurities of V20-2604 after 6 months at the accelerated condition in %
concepts.description: The total impurities, in %, of batch V20-2604 after 6 months at 40 °C/75 % RH

items.justification: Table 8, V20-2604 at 40 °C/75 % RH, gives 1.12 % of total impurities at 6 months.

concepts.name: Water content of V20-2604 after 12 months at the long-term condition in %
concepts.description: The water content, in %, of batch V20-2604 after 12 months at 25 °C/60 % RH

items.justification: Table 7, V20-2604 at 25 °C/60 % RH, gives a water content of 3.3 % at 12 months.

concepts.name: Assay of V20-2604 after 12 months at the intermediate condition in %
concepts.description: The assay, in % of the label claim, of batch V20-2604 after 12 months at 30 °C/65 % RH

items.justification: Table 9, V20-2604 at 30 °C/65 % RH, gives an assay of 98.1 % at 12 months.

aspects.name: Results outside the shelf-life specification
aspects.description: Identify the results of the study that do not meet the shelf-life specification, as the tables give them, the acceptance criteria that they fail, and the investigation of each in the report.

concepts.name: Tests with a result outside the shelf-life specification
concepts.description: Select every test with at least one result of any batch at any condition that does not meet the shelf-life specification

items.justification: Impurity D (V20-2604 and V20-2607 at 6 months, 40 °C/75 % RH), total impurities (V20-2604 at 6 months) and water content (V20-2604 at 3 and 6 months) exceed their limits; assay and dissolution stay within 92.0 % and 75 %.

concepts.name: Number of results outside the shelf-life specification
concepts.description: How many results of the study, counting each test of each batch at each condition and time point once, do not meet the shelf-life specification

items.justification: V20-2604 at 40 °C/75 % RH: water content of 4.4 % at 3 months and 5.6 % at 6 months (limit 4.0 %), impurity D of 0.41 % and total impurities of 1.12 % at 6 months; V20-2607 at 40 °C/75 % RH: impurity D of 0.31 % at 6 months (limit 0.30 %).

concepts.name: Every result outside the shelf-life specification is investigated in section 5
concepts.description: Whether section 5 reports an investigation of each result in the tables that does not meet the shelf-life specification

items.justification: INV-26-031 covers only the 6-month results of V20-2604 at the accelerated condition; its 3-month water content of 4.4 % and the 6-month impurity D of V20-2607 (0.31 %) are outside the specification but not investigated, and 5.5 says no other result was.

concepts.name: Root cause of the results of V20-2604 outside the shelf-life specification
concepts.description: The root cause that the investigation found for the results of batch V20-2604 that do not meet the shelf-life specification, in one sentence

items.value: Moisture ingress through the PVC film of the blister at 75 % RH, which raised the water content of the tablets and with it impurity D, a hydrolysis product.
items.justification: The root cause that 5.3 gives for the results of INV-26-031.
accepted_values: Moisture ingress through the PVC film of the blister at 75 % RH.
Moisture ingress through the PVC film of the blister.

aspects.name: Shelf-life rules and proposal
aspects.description: Identify the rules of the report for setting the shelf life, and the shelf life and the storage statement that it proposes for each container closure system.

concepts.name: Proposed shelf life of the PVC/Alu blister in months
concepts.description: The shelf life, in months, that the report proposes for the PVC/Alu blister

items.justification: Table 12 proposes 18 months for the PVC/Alu blister (V20-2604).

concepts.name: Storage statement of the PVC/Alu blister
concepts.description: The storage statement that the report proposes for the PVC/Alu blister, as worded in the report

items.value: Do not store above 25 °C. Store in the original package in order to protect from moisture.
items.justification: The storage statement that Table 12 proposes for the PVC/Alu blister.
accepted_values: Do not store above 25 °C; store in the original package in order to protect from moisture.

concepts.name: Rule that gives the proposed shelf life of the PVC/Alu blister
concepts.description: Select the rule of section 6 under which the proposed shelf life of the PVC/Alu blister is set

items.justification: 18 months is one and a half times the 12 months of long-term data (6.5), as 6.2 allows after a significant change at the accelerated condition only; 6.1 would allow 24 months and 6.3 12 months.
